## Implementation

Mapped the actual read-only `resume-check:<id>` dispatch to the existing run-level `ready` stage and added `resume-check` to `RUN_KINDS` so ordinary Codex names and Claude descriptions are mapped. Production change is exactly two classifier additions. `parseLabel`, `BEAD_KINDS`, `IN_SLOT`, coordinator behavior, schemas, timing windows and bounds remain unchanged.

The ID is the observed obligation, retained as the run-level suffix. It is not an implementation attempt. The current coordinator's `resumeCheckPrompt`, including its verification-only branch, forbids implementation, review, merge, closure, cleanup and editing. A successful or held observation therefore remains pre-admission observation. Classifying its duration as readiness work does not assert the obligation became ready: `readyAt` still derives from creation/mapping/dependency evidence.

Checked task17's advisory against the actual metric consumers. Adding this kind to `BEAD_KINDS` would create a per-bead attempt for the first associated event, change `at.start` and `dispatchedAt` to the observation, and extend ordinary `slotSpans` from that observation through the chain. Merely excluding `ready` from `IN_SLOT` does not avoid that ordinary-chain inflation. Run-level association preserves the obligation suffix without changing task identities, starts, attempts, readiness timestamps or slots. The regression compares complete bead JSON (including readiness) and task-slot JSON against unchanged profiles.

## Implemented

Process inspection failures now produce `unknown:` facts and exit 4. Failed ancestry, cwd/executable discovery, environment/orphan discovery, terminal inspection and termination inspection cannot become a verified empty sweep. A failed/empty per-PID status query requires successful authoritative PID enumeration proving disappearance before `stopped:` is emitted. TERM failure still receives status verification and, for an observably live process, a KILL attempt; survivors remain exit 3. Interactive preservation now returns exit 3. Existing cwd/executable, exact HOME/TMPDIR, orphan-argument matching, caller/ancestor protection and lack of kinship expansion remain in force. A macOS privileged login ancestor with hidden cwd is excluded only after successful ownership inspection proves it belongs to another user.

Worktree cleanup verifies the worktree and its temp root together before removing either. Sweep verifies its owned roots before any worktree/branch/temp deletion. Survivor, unknown and deliberate-retention outcomes retain resources and identify their paths, including --discard and --sweep. Dirty/unmerged guards remain. Missing-worktree discard also verifies owned roots before deleting its branch/temp state.

Finish returns `processSweep.stopped`, `survived`, `unknown`, `kept`, combines relevant facts from resource preflight and the final process sweep, and retains worktree/temp paths in `worktreesKept`. Null/scriptError sweep dispatch and missing processLines produce explicit unknowns rather than invented survivors or verified absence. Delivery completion remains separate. Merge, close-only, discard, ordinary-subagent Finish, run-state and Remaining report sources carry the same concrete helper contract. No replacement engine or broader matching was added.

rawSections.rawText:
## Implementation

Ordinary report-status now verifies every file in each latest retained collection record against its saved SHA-256. Missing, unreadable or non-file artifacts add an invocation/path-specific archive-unavailable gap; changed bytes add an integrity-mismatch gap. An affected collection is pending even if its saved complete flag remains true. The existing acceptance delegation consumes these qualifiers and therefore refuses acceptance without a mutating recollection. Status reads never rewrite collection records, archives or source bundles. Existing persisted gaps and independent acceptance obligations remain effective.

The focused test uses real --collect, ordinary status and --acceptance commands. It independently deletes and corrupts the direct review, direct .md.diff, cluster review, assembled clusters manifest, assembled slice and declared required input. It verifies complete matching archives remain eligible before and after source cleanup, requires specific integrity gaps for all twelve damaged states, and preserves a separate pending human decision. Before/after snapshots compare exact bytes (stronger than their hashes), mtimes, mode and directory inventory for run text, archives and fixture sources. ## Implementation

The shared temporary-directory fixture now applies Node's built-in path.resolve to the directory returned by mktemp before deriving expected artifact paths. This matches the dispatch consumer's lexical directory spelling without resolving symlinks to a different physical prefix. The only tracked change is two added lines in tests/super-code/test-dispatch-text.sh. No production code or assertion changed.

All invocation-specific filenames and equality assertions remain intact. The existing caller-advance fixture and prior-bundle-content fixture still execute in each full targeted suite; both passed in all three final configurations. An incorrect task ordinal, dispatch label, invocation identity, captured Git source, or overwritten prior bundle would still fail the existing assertions.

rawSections.rawText:
## Implementation

The prior real-builder fixture reproduced the root cause: a persisted invocation ID owned fixed assembly/review paths, but Finish captured a newer integration head on resume and neither Launch nor compact Recovery facts bound the ID to its reviewed source.

The existing `dispatch-text.mjs` now provides `bind-review-source`: it persists a compact existing Recovery deferred record carrying `data.reviewSource` with invocationId/base/head, or reads/verifies the existing binding. It accepts captured Launch facts too. Same-ID source mismatch, invalid/conflicting facts, an existing unbound bundle, and attempts to write existing outputs or direct `.diff` packages are refused without replacing partial bytes. `--read` retrieves an existing binding without capturing a new tip. Rendering dispatch text alone is not represented as persistence.

Workflow Finish reads the original compact binding from its existing Resume/Finish digest observations before selecting review inputs. Every existing final assembly, single, cluster, seam and stub producer runs the shared binding guard before writing artifacts. No dispatch was added. A source-guard refusal keeps final review unavailable with `reviewPath: null`, preserving the partial bundle rather than bypassing its findings through direct review. Ordinary assembler unavailability retains the existing direct-input fallback. New invocation IDs can capture newer source independently. Both coordinator instruction paths explain this contract. Existing finding lifecycle and identity/cause handling were not changed. The omitted-ID startup repair owned by task .23 was not touched.
